capabilities: Run Codex CLI prompts from a sidebar, workspace tab, or pop-out window
Queue and guide follow-up prompts while a Codex run is active
Insert current-note context and @-suggest vault Markdown files
Select model, reasoning effort, and file-access sandbox per run
Manage reusable prompt templates in a library
extras: Desktop-only because mobile Obsidian cannot launch local CLI processes. Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Warns before YOLO (danger-full-access) runs and before running non-codex commands; third-party keys require Obsidian 1.11.4+ native secret storage and are not written to data.json.
motivation: The README says it is built for users who want to ask Codex for help while staying in Obsidian, with the vault as the working context.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to run Codex agent sessions with the vault as working context, forcing users to leave the app or a terminal.

relations.evidence: the local codex CLI as the execution engine
Zhipu uses a current locally installed Claude Code CLI

requires.name: Third-party provider API keys (MiniMax, Kimi, DeepSeek, Zhipu)

summary: Sidebar, workspace-tab, and pop-out interface for running the local Codex CLI inside Obsidian, with streaming Markdown answers and vault context.
